concepts.label: Single Query Transaction - a transaction consisting of exactly one SQL++ query and no key-value operations, run via `QueryOptions.asTransaction()` (or `singleQueryTransactionOptions()`), used to avoid the Query service's per-document in-memory state overhead during large bulk-loading workloads
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a lighter-weight, structurally restricted variant of sdk:distributed-transaction (no lambda, no `ctx`, no retries of application logic - just a single call with an `asTransaction()` flag), not the same shape as the full transaction API, so not simply an instance of it either.

concepts.label: `tximplicit` query parameter - the underlying N1QL query option that single query transactions set internally to mark a statement as its own implicit transaction
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - placeholder for a server/N1QL-side query parameter referenced but not documented on this page; not yet extracted in any round

relations.subject: sdk:single-query-transaction
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused predicate; directionality is single-query-transaction preferred over a full multi-statement transaction specifically for large bulk-loading workloads, to avoid Query-service memory pressure
relations.evidence: The Query service maintains where required some in-memory state for each document in a transaction, that is freed on commit or rollback. For most use-cases this presents no issue, but there are some workloads, such as bulk loading many documents, where this could exceed the server resources allocated to the service. Solutions to this include breaking the workload up into smaller batches, and allocating additional memory to the Query service. Alternatively, single query transaction, described here, may be used.

cross_component_finding: The DurabilityLevel enum (Majority/PersistToMajority/etc.) now recurs at a THIRD distinct scope in this batch alone: per-key-value-operation (sdk:durability, kv-operations.md), per-transaction-config (sdk:transaction-durability, distributed-acid-transactions-from-the-sdk.md), and now per-single-query-transaction-call (this page). All three reuse the identical enum values but are configured through three separate, non-interchangeable API surfaces (InsertOptions.durability(), TransactionsConfig.durabilityLevel(), singleQueryTransactionOptions().durabilityLevel()). This is a clean, repeated confirmation of the round's hypothesis: the vocabulary is shared at the enum-value level but the SCOPE at which durability applies is a genuinely new axis introduced by the transactions feature, not present at all in the pre-transactions vocabulary.
